newsitem.title: USA: NYS senator report details underwriters' donations.
newsitem.headline: NYS senator report details underwriters' donations.

text.p: New York State Sen. Franz Leichter on Wednesday issued a report that drew links between donations made by underwriters to state Republicans and local committees, alleging the gifts helped the firms win contracts.
The following list details some of the specific allegations that Leichter, a Manhattan Democrat, made:

-- Goldman Sachs gave $21,500 to political committees controlled by the state GOP, including two $1,000 donations to Republican State Supreme Court candidates. Leichter said: "It is unheard of for a municipal bond firm like Goldman Sachs to make contributions to judicial candidates."
He added Goldman was the top municipal underwriter in the state, citing its G-37 filings, that he said showed it was chosen for 76 bond issues in the 1996 fourth quarter.

-- PaineWebber Inc gave $8,000 to the Republican State Committee's housekeeping account in 1996. The firm's president, Joseph Grano and his wife gave another $6,666 last year. The firm said it underwrote 12 New York State bond issues in the fourth quarter of 1996, according to Leichter.

-- First Albany Corp's chief executive officer gave $10,000 to the Republican State Committee, $1,000 to the Senate Republican Campaign Committee, and $3,000 to the Committee to Elect Joseph Bruno. The last amount was disputed by an off-the-record source close to the firm.
The firm underwrote 23 state bond issues during the period, Leichter said.
-- Dillon Read gave a $10,000 contribution to the Republican State Committee, and underwrote seven municipal bond issues during the period, up from two in the first quarter.
-- Carmona Motley and Co. gave $1,500 to the Republican State Committee's housekeeping account, and underwrote two municipal bond issues in the fourth quarter of 1996.

-- Artemis Capital Group gave $1,000 to the Monroe County Republican Party, and underwrote two bond issues in the period. The firm, in its G-37 filing, said it "obtained a letter from the party attesting that this money will be used strictly for operating purposes and will not be used on behalf of any candidates or political events," Leichter said.
-- Roosevelt & Cross gave $500 to the Nassau County Republican Committee, $540 to the Long Beach City Republican Committee, and $300 to the Huntington Republican Committee.

The firm also reported giving $3,100 to the New York State Conservative Party, $500 to the Republican State Committee's housekeeping account, and $250 to the Republican Assembly Campaign Committee, the state senator said.

In fourth quarter 1996, the firm said it got municipal bond business from Nassau County, the Town of Huntington, the Town of Lewiston, the Town of Hanover, the Babylon Industrial Development Authority, the Village of Black River, and the Islip Community Development Agency, according to Leichter.
